title: FSSAI Suspends Licences of Five Nutraceutical Makers Over Safety Violations
excerpt: Vedant Remedies scored 12% on compliance and two makers were not operating from their licensed premises at all, the food regulator said, suspending all five licences with immediate effect.
body:
• India's food regulator FSSAI on Monday suspended the licences of five nutraceutical and health supplement makers with immediate effect: Vedant Remedies, Lucid Health Care, Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare, Vitamedic Health Nutraceuticals and Adorreal Healthcare.
  • Vedant Remedies scored just 12% on compliance, Lucid Health Care 27% and Ambico 46%, according to the regulator — findings included expired flavouring substances and materials, poor hygiene and faulty pest control.
  • Vitamedic had shifted from its licensed premises without endorsement — to premises shared with a meat-processing unit — and Adorreal's licensed premises were non-operational, with construction underway.
  • For consumers: the suspensions are of manufacturing licences. If you use supplements from these five makers, check the maker name on the label — FSSAI's announcement does not name individual products or order a recall.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has suspended the licences of five nutraceutical and health supplement manufacturers over serious safety violations, the regulator said on Monday. The five are Vedant Remedies, Lucid Health Care Pvt Ltd, Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare, Vitamedic Health Nutraceuticals and Adorreal Healthcare, and the suspensions take immediate effect.

""The shifted premises was also found to be shared with another active food processing unit, M/s Myyo Foods India Private Limited, engaged in meat processing," it added."

What inspectors found, company by company

At Vedant Remedies Pvt Ltd, FSSAI said it found poor hygiene, damaged infrastructure, lack of proper storage, expired food flavouring substances and a lack of food safety records. Reporting of the same announcement by IANS adds that AYUSH-licensed and FSSAI-licensed ingredients were inadequately segregated, creating a cross-contamination risk, that products were being manufactured without a valid food licence, and that the unit scored 12% on compliance.

At Lucid Health Care, the regulator found poor hygiene, inadequate lighting, improper storage and faulty pest control. Ayurvedic and nutraceutical products were manufactured within the same premises with inadequate segregation and storage, food handlers lacked proper hygiene facilities, protective equipment and mandatory FoSTaC training, and mandatory food safety, testing and maintenance records were not properly maintained. IANS reported a compliance score of 27% for the facility.

Ambico Ayurvedic Healthcare's premises were found lacking in hygiene and sanitation, among other violations; IANS reported unsanitary premises, expired materials stored on site, absent mandatory food safety and testing records, and a compliance score of 46%.

The two premises that were not operating as licensed

Vitamedic Health Nutraceuticals had shifted from its licensed premises without endorsement of the new address on its FSSAI licence, FSSAI said in its account carried by The Hindu BusinessLine. "The shifted premises was also found to be shared with another active food processing unit, M/s Myyo Foods India Private Limited, engaged in meat processing," it added.

Adorreal Healthcare's licensed premises were found non-operational, with construction work underway. The company continued to hold an active FSSAI licence against a non-existent or disposed premises and was found to have furnished false or misleading information. "Due to serious regulatory violations, the FSSAI license of M/s. ADORREAL HEALTHCARE has been suspended with immediate effect under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said in its social media post.

What this means for supplement buyers

The action is part of what IANS described as the regulator's ongoing efforts to strengthen compliance and consumer safety in the fast-growing nutraceutical industry. The announcement suspends manufacturing licences; it does not list individual products, batches or a recall. Readers who buy health supplements made in India — including diaspora shoppers who stock up on visits home — can check the manufacturer name printed on the label against the five named above.
